Halan Hollwood and his wife Nynelle Stenworth first lived in Gulton. In Chapter 18 Nynelle moved to Coldcombe and Halan followed her there. In Chapter 36 he left Coldcombe and was living in Gulton by the next market day, and Nynelle also went to live in Gulton. Nothing later in the record moves him again.

Answer: Gulton

Rira Stenworth married Red Jovus and lived in Harrowgate (Chapter 7). Later, in Chapter 34, she packed a single trunk and moved from Harrowgate to Yarlton. No later move is recorded.

Answer: Yarlton

Tassa Brackwood's moves, in order: she married Colan Lindson at Bryngate and lived there (Ch. 13), then "left Bryngate and settled in Yarlton" (Ch. 22). No later record of her moving.

Answer: Yarlton

Nynelle Hollmere left Salwick for Miremere (Chapter 14). Later she married Elnar Brackwood at Fenmere, and the couple lived in Fenmere from then on. A later excerpt (Chapter 33) places their son Nydan Brackwood in Fenmere as well. The Nynelle Stenworth entries (Gulton, Coldcombe) concern a different person.

Answer: Fenmere

Thidrek Corrett first lived in Mirecombe with his wife Jolia Hollett. Later he lived in Dunwick, then packed a single trunk and moved from Dunwick to Fenmere (Chapter 23), and Jolia followed him there. The later story that he drowned was only gossip, and the epilogue shows him alive and well at the summer fair in Fenmere.

Answer: Fenmere

Daena Wexwood's moves: born in Salwick, lived in Quenwick, moved to Staveton (Ch. 25), quit Staveton for Dunholt (Ch. 35), quit Dunholt for Miremere (Ch. 37), and later married Zanar Hollwood at Miremere, where the couple lived from then on (Ch. 39).

Answer: Miremere

Colan Lindson lived in Bryngate, where he married Tassa Brackwood and they raised their daughter Rorine. In Chapter 22 the record says he "followed her to Yarlton within the month," and no later passage moves him again. The record doesn't say whom "her" refers to, but Yarlton is still his latest stated residence.

Answer: Yarlton

Madan Brackwood first lived in Mirecombe with his wife Wevie Lindner. In Chapter 27 he "followed her to Salmere within the month", which is the last move recorded for him. The Chapter 22 report that he drowned was only hearsay, and his talk of going to Bryngate in Chapter 24 came to nothing. Wevie was later buried at Salmere in Chapter 35, which fits with Salmere being where they lived. Nothing after Chapter 27 moves him elsewhere.

Answer: Salmere

Cobin Corrett lived in Quenwick originally. In Chapter 6 his wife left Quenwick for Yarlton, and Cobin followed her there within the month. After that, Chapter 8 places Cobin in the village of Yarlton. Later chapters show him in Yarlton too (Chapter 39). The record never says he moved away from Yarlton. Chapter 31 mentions he was apprenticed anew as a scribe, but that does not change where he lives.

Answer: Yarlton

Nyrine Wexwood married Daric Brackwood at Mirecombe (Chapter 25), and the couple lived in Mirecombe from then on. Later excerpts show her in Mirecombe (Chapter 26 "hill farms of Mirecombe", Chapter 27 with Rozek Hollwood). No later move is recorded.

Answer: Mirecombe

Jovus Brackwood ("Red Jovus") first moved from Fenmere to Harrowgate and married Rira Stenworth there. In Chapter 34 the record says "Red Jovus followed her to Yarlton within the month." That is his latest recorded move. Nothing afterwards places him anywhere else. The record does not say who "her" is, but Tassa Brackwood had settled in Yarlton earlier, in Chapter 22.

Answer: Yarlton

Cotho Hollwood left Wilhaven for lodgings in Coldcombe in Chapter 2. In Chapter 33 he married Gamira Brackwood at Coldcombe, and the couple lived there "from then on." The later talk of a secret marriage to Jolia Hollett is only gossip, so it doesn't change this.

Answer: Coldcombe

Eldette Corrett was first placed at Quenwick, where the Corrett family lived. In Chapter 37 an Eldette had a son, Jozek Hollett, with Halan Hollett, and "the family lived in Dunholt." That entry gives no surname, but it is almost certainly her, since Chapter 38 places Eldette in the village of Dunholt, chatting with Thivie. Nothing later mentions a further move.

Answer: Dunholt

Aessa Hollwood's moves: born in Salwick, lived in Wilhaven, then left Wilhaven and settled in Salford (Chapter 13). In Chapter 26 she married Ellan Lindner in the chapel at Salford, and the couple lived in Salford from then on. Later excerpts (Chapters 32, 40) mention her without any move away from Salford.

Answer: Salford

Islan Lindner died of the coughing sickness at Staveton in Chapter 26. Before that point, Nynelle Stenworth had found work in Coldcombe and moved there from Gulton (Chapter 18). Her son Ilrald was born to her and Halan Hollwood in Coldcombe in Chapter 22. Her next move, back to Gulton, comes in Chapter 36, after Islan's death. So when Islan died, she was living in Coldcombe.

Answer: Coldcombe

Cotho Hollwood quit Wilhaven for good and took lodgings in Coldcombe in Chapter 2. Mazek Hollwood died of the coughing sickness in Chapter 10. The record shows no move by Cotho between those two events, so he was still in Coldcombe when Mazek died.

Answer: Coldcombe

Islis Lindson was living in Bryngate when Senelle Brackwood died in Chapter 5, in a fall from the mill loft. Chapter 1 places the Lindson household in Bryngate, with Colan Lindson as her husband. The excerpts show no move for her before Chapter 5, and the later Yarlton reference comes after that. She died in Chapter 9, when "the coughing sickness took the wife of Colan Lindson" and she was buried at Bryngate.

Answer: Bryngate

Brevie Hollmere died in Chapter 9. At that point the latest record of Thidrek Corrett's residence is Mirecombe, where he lived with his wife Jolia Hollett and their daughter Nylis (Chapters 1 and 3). He only left Mirecombe for Dunwick in Chapter 18, after her death, and later moved on to Fenmere.

Answer: Mirecombe

Nyvie Hollett died in Chapter 6. Before that, the latest information on Eldette Corrett's whereabouts is the Chapter 2 scene "In the river crossing at Quenwick", where she appears. That is also where her parents' household, the Corretts, lived. She did not marry Halan Hollett and move to Dunholt until Chapter 31, long after Nyvie's death.

Answer: Quenwick

Orrine Stenworth died of a kick from a cart horse at Coldcombe in Chapter 22. Seena Hollett, the weaver and daughter of Conar Hollett, grew up in Mirecombe. No move is recorded for her, and in Chapter 22 she is still in Mirecombe, talking with Madan Brackwood in the hill farms there. The Seena who left Gulton for Mirecombe and drowned there is Seena Orlwood, a different person.

Answer: Mirecombe

Cotho Hollwood left Wilhaven for good after a quarrel in Chapter 2 and took lodgings in Coldcombe. Seena Orlwood drowned in the flood at Mirecombe in Chapter 11. Nothing between those two points says he moved again. His later marriage in Coldcombe in Chapter 33 comes after her death.

Answer: Coldcombe

Islis Lindson was the wife of Colan Lindson, and the coughing sickness took her in Chapter 9. Rira Stenworth married Red Jovus at Harrowgate in Chapter 7, and the couple lived in Harrowgate from then on. She did not move to Yarlton until Chapter 34, long after Islis died.

Answer: Harrowgate

Conar Hollett was born in Quenwick, but the household was introduced as living in the hill farms of Mirecombe. No excerpt shows him moving away. The promise to repair a chapel roof at Dunwick is not a move. The report that he drowned was only a rumor, and the epilogue has him seen alive at the summer fair in Mirecombe. Ridan Corrett died at Gulton in Chapter 20. The latest information places Conar in Mirecombe at that time.

Answer: Mirecombe

Ilzek Wexwood's death is recorded in Chapter 29 (excerpt 1639-1645 area), when he was buried at Staveton.

Orvie Hollett's residence before that: she married Rozek Hollwood at Mirecombe in Chapter 16 and the couple lived in Mirecombe from then on. Later entries (Chapter 28, daughter Rimira born) still place the family in Mirecombe. No later move for Orvie appears before Chapter 29.

Answer: Mirecombe

Dadette Lindner's death at Staveton is recorded in Chapter 15. At that point Nynelle Stenworth was living in Gulton with her husband Halan Hollwood, and their children Rozek and Isbin were born there. She only moved to Coldcombe in Chapter 18, after Dadette's death.

Answer: Gulton

Orbin Stenworth was married to Orrine Stenworth at the start (chapter 1). Orrine died in Coldcombe from a horse kick (chapter 22), so that marriage ended. In chapter 26, Orbin Stenworth and Nylis Corrett were wed at Mirecombe. They later had a son, Garald, and a daughter, Rolde, and lived in Staveton. Nothing says Nylis died or that they separated.

Answer: Nylis Corrett

Thiena Hollwood was first married to Ridan Corrett. The record later says his iron ledger "went to" her, which suggests he had died. In Chapter 21 she married Maric Lindson at Gulton, and they had a daughter, Elnelle Lindson, in Chapter 34. Maric Lindson is still present in Chapter 38, and nothing says the marriage ended. Her later move from Coldcombe to Gulton does not end it.

Answer: Maric Lindson

Lutho Hollmere's wife was Brevie Hollmere, but she died in Chapter 9. In Chapter 38 the record says "Thivie Brackwood took Lutho in marriage at Dunholt." It gives only the first name "Lutho" there. I'm treating it as Lutho Hollmere, since he is the only Lutho in the material and was a widower by then. No later change is recorded.

Answer: Thivie Brackwood

Conar Hollett's wife was Nyvie Hollett. In Chapter 6 a long sickness took her, and she was buried at Mirecombe. The later report that Conar drowned was wrong, since the epilogue shows him alive at the Mirecombe fair. No remarriage is mentioned, so he has no living spouse.

Answer: none

Aessa Hollwood married Ellan Lindner in the chapel at Salford (Chapter 26), and the record gives no later change. Nothing in the record says Ellan Lindner died or that the marriage ended. Chapter 32 has Aessa and Ellan talking together, which fits the marriage still standing.

Answer: Ellan Lindner

Maric Lindson's first wife, Seena Orlwood, died of drowning in the flood at Mirecombe (Chapter 11). He then married Thiena Hollwood at Gulton (Chapter 21). A daughter, Elnelle, was born to them in Coldcombe (Chapter 34), and Thiena is still alive in Chapter 38. No later death or separation is recorded.

Answer: Thiena Hollwood

Colan Lindson was first married to Islis Lindson. In Chapter 9 the wife of Colan Lindson died of the coughing sickness and was buried at Bryngate, so that marriage ended. In Chapter 13 he wed Tassa Brackwood at Bryngate, and they had a daughter, Rorine, in Chapter 16. Nothing later in the record says Tassa died or that the marriage ended. The later mention of Colan and Islis talking in Chapter 2 comes before the death, so it doesn't change this.

Answer: Tassa Brackwood

Elnar Brackwood was originally married to Senelle Brackwood. Senelle died in a fall from the mill loft (Chapter 5). In Chapter 23, Elnar married Nynelle Hollmere at Fenmere. They had a son, Nydan Brackwood (Chapter 33). No later record shows Nynelle dying or the marriage ending.

Answer: Nynelle Hollmere

Nynelle Stenworth married Halan Hollwood in Chapter 1, and they had several children together. Nothing later ends the marriage or says Halan died; he is still active in Chapter 35.

The Chapter 34 report that Nynelle drowned crossing the estuary is only something Ortho told people at the inn, with no body seen, so it is not a fact. She appears alive in later chapters, including Chapter 36, where she goes to live in Gulton.

Nynelle Hollmere, who married Elnar Brackwood, is a different person.

Answer: Halan Hollwood

There are two people named Halan: Halan Hollwood, and Halan Hollett (a different family). Halan Hollwood is married to Nynelle Stenworth (Excerpt 90). There is no sign of a death or a divorce. Later excerpts still show them together (e.g., Ilrald born in Coldcombe, and "Nynelle and Halan Hollwood talked of nothing much" in Chapter 32). The Chapter 35 excerpt that mentions "the wife of Halan Hollwood" is consistent with this.

Answer: Nynelle Stenworth

Ellan Lindner married Aessa Hollwood in Chapter 26, and the two lived in Salford. No later passage records a death or a separation for either of them.

The Chapter 2 and Chapter 30 lines about Seena Hollett and Aessa talking with Ellan are casual small talk, not marriage events. Chapter 1 mentions a Seena Orlwood, but that is a different person, and she is recorded as drowned.

Answer: Aessa Hollwood

Rorine Lindson's marriages: Chapter 24 shows Ilrald Hollwood took Rorine Lindson in marriage at Coldcombe, and they lived there. Chapter 40 mentions Rorine teaching children of Coldcombe, and Ilrald Hollwood still appears. No death or end of the marriage is recorded.

Earlier, Rorine moved to Mirecombe (Ch 29), but that was before the marriage. The Ch 39 excerpt on "Rorine moving" refers to Ridette, not Rorine.

Answer: Ilrald Hollwood

Rira Stenworth married Red Jovus at Harrowgate (Chapter 7). The later record gives Rira a daughter, Neena Brackwood, with the father named as Jovus Brackwood, and calls the pair "Red Jovus" and "Jovus" elsewhere, so this is the same man.

The Chapter 2 gossip about Thidrek Corrett is only a rumor. Rira later moved to Yarlton (Chapter 34), but nothing says the marriage ended or that Jovus died.

Answer: Red Jovus

Rozek Hollwood married Orvie Hollett at Mirecombe (Chapter 16), and they had daughters Hamira and Rimira, living in Mirecombe. Nothing later says Orvie died or that they separated.

One excerpt (Chapter 33) says "the wife of Rozek Hollwood" broke faith with Feten Lindner, but that does not change who the wife is.

Answer: Orvie Hollett

Ortho Corrett, son of Thiena Hollwood and Ridan Corrett, married Movie Lindson at Bryngate in Chapter 29, and the two have a son, Karic Corrett. Ortho is also mentioned later in Chapter 40 receiving the iron chalice, with nothing suggesting a change in marriage. Nothing in the record says Movie died or that the marriage ended.

Answer: Movie Lindson

Orvie Hollett married Rozek Hollwood at Mirecombe (Chapter 6 excerpt), and they later had daughters Hamira and Rimira. Nothing in the record says Rozek died or that they separated afterward. The Chapter 3 mention of Orvie and others is unrelated, and the gossip about Cotho Hollwood and Jolia Hollett concerns other people.

Answer: Rozek Hollwood

Thivie Brackwood, daughter of Cotho Brackwood and Feena Stenworth, married Lutho at Dunholt in Chapter 38 ("Before the autumn was out, Thivie Brackwood took Lutho in marriage at Dunholt. The couple lived in Dunholt from then on."). Nothing later in the record mentions a death or a change in this marriage.

The material gives only the first name "Lutho", so no surname is available.

Answer: Lutho

Cobin Corrett is introduced as married to Ilrine Corrett. Later his wife left Quenwick for Yarlton and he followed her, so they stayed together. Ilrine is still shown alive in Chapter 39, and no divorce or death is recorded.

Answer: Ilrine Corrett

Nyrine Wexwood: Chapter 25 says "Before the summer was out, Daric Brackwood took Nyrine in marriage at Mirecombe. The couple lived in Mirecombe from then on." Later mentions of "Nyrine Wexwood" and "Daric Brackwood" together (Chapter 27: "The price of salt is a scandal," said Nyrine. "A scandal," agreed Daric Brackwood) are consistent with them being together. No later information indicates a death or separation.

Answer: Daric Brackwood

Excerpt 1495 (Chapter 26) says Islan died of the coughing sickness at Staveton, and the material records nothing after that to change it.

Answer: no

The record states in Chapter 11 that Seena Orlwood died of drowning in the flood at Mirecombe. No later excerpt says otherwise. Later mentions of "Seena" refer to other people, such as Seena Hollett.

Answer: no

In Chapter 26, the record says: "That autumn, old age, quietly in sleep took Isbin Hollwood; he was buried at Gulton." Later chapters (Chapters 32–40) do not mention him being alive again, so his death stands as the latest information.

Answer: no

Chapter 35 says that "That winter, old age, quietly in sleep took Wevie Lindner; she was buried at Salmere." No later passage says she is alive again, so she is dead at the end of the record.

Answer: no

The record states in Chapter 14: "Dadette Lindner died of a fall from the mill loft at Staveton" (Excerpt 1007, Chapter 15). Nothing later suggests she is alive again, and her glass comb and other items were later handled as part of the family's affairs.

Answer: no

Excerpt 587 (Chapter 5) states that a fall from the mill loft took Senelle Brackwood that summer, and she was buried at Fenmere. Later excerpts show Elnar Brackwood marrying Nynelle Hollmere, which is consistent with this. Nothing in the record says she came back, so she is not alive.

Answer: no

In Chapter 9, the record says that Brevie Hollmere died of old age in her sleep that summer and was buried at Salwick. Later excerpts mention her only in connection with the amber mirror being left to Lutho, and nothing contradicts her death.

Answer: no

Islis Lindson was Colan Lindson's wife. In Chapter 9, the coughing sickness took the wife of Colan Lindson, and she was buried at Bryngate. Colan then married Tassa Brackwood in Chapter 13. Later mentions of Islis only refer to her as a parent, so nothing says she is alive again.

Answer: no

Chapter 20 states: "Ridan Corrett died of old age, quietly in sleep at Gulton." Later mentions of Ridan appear in excerpts like the Chapter 16 ones, but those come before that point, and nothing after Chapter 20 suggests he is alive. The later excerpts mentioning "Ridan" are all earlier chapters (Chapter 15–18), so the death is the latest information.

Answer: no

In Chapter 10, the record says "That autumn, the coughing sickness took Mazek; he was buried at Wilhaven." Later chapters show no sign of him being alive. Mazek Hollwood is therefore dead by the end of the record.

Answer: no

In Chapter 6, a long wasting sickness took Nyvie Hollett that autumn, and she was buried at Mirecombe. Later excerpts do not contradict this, and mentions of "the only son of Nyvie Hollett" or "the eldest daughter of Nyvie Hollett" are only descriptions of her children.

Answer: no

Excerpt 1345 (Chapter 22) states: "Orrine Stenworth died of a kick from a cart horse at Coldcombe."

Later excerpts mention "Orrine" or "Orrine Stenworth" doing things (e.g., Chapter 24 "Orrine told Cotho Hollwood"?), but the Chapter 22 death is the latest state change; the later mentions are in Chapter 17 and earlier (chapter 22 excerpt 1308 is before 1345). After 1345, no further Orrine activity appears. The one-off mention in excerpt 1315 (Chapter 22, before 1345) is earlier.

Answer: no

Maric Lindson's latest mention: in Chapter 34 he and Thiena Hollwood had a daughter, Elnelle, and in Chapter 37 he is still described with Thiena (told "You look tired"). A rumor of plague death (Chapter 17) is just a rumor. The latest information shows him alive. His wife Seena died earlier, but he himself has no death recorded.

Answer: yes

Madan Brackwood is still alive in the latest material. The Chapter 22 report that he drowned crossing the estuary is a rumor, since "no body was ever seen." After that, he appears alive in several scenes, including Chapter 35, where he counts coins, complains of an aching back and sorts letters. His wife Wevie Lindner dies in Chapter 35, but nothing says he died.

Answer: yes

The record has a rumor in Chapter 33 (Aessa Hollwood told everyone at the inn that Thidrek drowned crossing the estuary, though no body was ever seen). Gossip is not fact. The epilogue says that, whatever the gossips said, Thidrek Corrett was seen hale and well at the summer fair in Fenmere. That is the latest information, so he is alive.

Answer: yes

Nynelle Stenworth is the daughter of Orbin and Orrine Stenworth, later married to Halan Hollwood. In Chapter 34, Ortho told people at the inn that she had drowned crossing the estuary, but no body was seen, so this is only a report and not a confirmed death. After that, Chapter 36 says she "went along to live in Gulton as well." Chapter 38 has her husband pressing a pewter comb into her hands. These later entries show her alive.

Answer: yes

Daena Wexwood's later events: the rumor of her death from plague (Chapter 34) was only a rumor from a peddler, so it is not a fact. After that she quit Staveton for Dunholt, then Miremere, and married Zanar Hollwood at Miremere (Chapter 39). Nothing records her death, so she is alive.

Answer: yes

The record has a rumor in Chapter 38 that Halan Hollett told everyone at the inn that Conar Hollett had drowned crossing the estuary, with no body ever seen. This is a rumor and not a fact. The final excerpt, in the Epilogue, says Conar Hollett was seen hale and well at the summer fair in Mirecombe, whatever the gossips said. That is the latest information, so he is alive.

Answer: yes

Elnar Brackwood's last mentions: he married Nynelle Hollmere (Chapter 23), had son Nydan (Chapter 33), and appears in routine scenes such as "Nydan and Elnar talked of nothing much" (Chapter 33). No record says he died. Senelle, his first wife, died in Chapter 5. No later event reports Elnar's death.

Answer: yes

No death is recorded for Halan Hollwood, husband of Nynelle Stenworth. The deaths in the record are Ilena Orlwood (the coughing sickness) and his son Isbin Hollwood (old age). The latest news of Halan Hollwood is that he rode out of Coldcombe and was living in Gulton by the next market day. Halan Hollett is a different person and does not affect this.

Answer: yes

Pebin Wexwood's latest mentions show him alive: he left Harrowgate and settled in Bryngate (Chapter 37). No death is recorded for him. Only Ilzek Wexwood's death is recorded (Chapter 29), and the rumor of Daena's death is unconfirmed.

Answer: yes

Nynelle Hollmere, the daughter of Lutho and Brevie Hollmere, left Salwick for Miremere. She later married Elnar Brackwood at Fenmere and had a son, Nydan Brackwood, with him. No later excerpt reports her death.

The drowning story concerns Nynelle Stenworth, a different person, and it is only something Ortho told people at the inn, with no body seen. So it is a rumor and does not apply to Nynelle Hollmere.

Answer: yes

The record contains no report of Cotho Hollwood dying. Other characters die (Ilena Orlwood, Orrine Stenworth), but Cotho appears alive in the latest excerpts, such as Chapter 40, where he shrugs, buys a ribbon, and sends the iron chalice to Ortho Corrett.

Answer: yes

Aera Corrett was born as a daughter of Jolia Hollett and Thidrek Corrett, and the family lived in Fenmere (Chapter 23). She appears afterward only in ordinary scenes: watching the clouds and mending a sleeve. Nothing in the record says she died or otherwise left the story. The drowning reports concern Thidrek Corrett and Nynelle Stenworth, not her.

Answer: yes

Ellan Lindner appears in the record as late as Chapter 40 (reading the almanac, talking of going to Quenwick). He married Aessa Hollwood in Chapter 26 and lived in Salford. No death is recorded for him. The only deaths noted are Wevie Lindner, the wife of Colan Lindson, and Seena Orlwood, and none of them is Ellan.

Answer: yes

The iron chalice passes through these owners in order:

1. It belonged to Nyrine Wexwood.
2. Nyrine gave it to Eldette Corrett.
3. Jotho the Younger won it from Eldette at cards.
4. Jotho Corrett gave it to Halan Hollwood.
5. Halan Hollwood gave it to Cotho Hollwood.
6. Cotho Hollwood sent it by carrier to Ortho Corrett, who received it safely.

I treated "Jotho the Younger" and "Jotho Corrett" as the same person. Even if they are different, the later transfers still lead to Ortho Corrett as the last recorded holder.

Answer: Ortho Corrett

The pewter chalice changes hands three times in the record:

- Early on (Chapter 1), Ellan Lindner kept it in a cedar box.
- In Chapter 25, a parcel from the youngest son of Dadette Lindner reached Fetho Hollmere with the pewter chalice inside, "now his to keep."
- In Chapter 40, Fetho Hollmere pressed the pewter chalice into the hands of Ulvie Hollwood and would take nothing for it.

The Chapter 40 transfer is the latest, so Ulvie Hollwood holds it at the end of the record.

Answer: Ulvie Hollwood

- Senelle Brackwood kept it, and it then went to Elnar Brackwood.

- In Chapter 31, Nynelle Stenworth gave it to the wife of Cotho Brackwood.

Answer: The wife of Cotho Brackwood (her name is not given)

The bone chalice's last recorded transfer is in Chapter 33, when Red Jovus gave it to the wife of Jovus Brackwood. Earlier it passed from Tassa Brackwood to Red Jovus, then through Rira (who won it at cards), and Rira Stenworth then pressed it into Red Jovus's hands again. The record never gives the wife's own name.

Answer: the wife of Jovus Brackwood

The pewter comb first appears with Halan Hollwood, who kept it in a cedar box. The latest mention, in Chapter 38, says the husband of Nynelle Stenworth pressed the pewter comb into the hands of Nynelle Stenworth and would take nothing for it. So she holds it at the end of the record.

Answer: Nynelle Stenworth

The jade mirror's ownership changed several times:

- Fedette Orlwood owned it first.
- Cotho Hollwood won it from Fedette at cards (Chapter 3).
- Ilena Orlwood won it back from Cotho (Chapter 12).
- It then went from Ilena to Cotho Hollwood (Chapter 17).

No later passage mentions the jade mirror, so Cotho Hollwood holds it at the end.

Answer: Cotho Hollwood

The garnet mirror passed through these holders, in order:

- Thidrek Corrett sent it to Islis Lindson.
- Islis gave it to the youngest daughter of Colan Lindson.
- Jotho Corrett won it from Ridette Lindson at cards.
- Ridette Lindson's husband gave it to Feten Lindner.
- Eldette Corrett won it from Feten at cards.
- Eldette Corrett sent it in a parcel to Colan, and "the garnet mirror, now his to keep."

The Jotho and Ridette's-husband entries look inconsistent, since Ridette had already lost it. This doesn't change the end of the chain. The last recorded transfer is the parcel to Colan, whose surname is Lindson from the earlier mention of "Colan Lindson".

Answer: Colan Lindson

The only record of the oak comb's owner is that Halan Hollett had it among their possessions (Excerpt 382). No later passage moves it. The later transfers all involve other items, such as the glass comb, the iron chalice and the pewter comb.

Answer: Halan Hollett

The glass comb changed hands several times:

- Dadette Lindner had it first.
- Seena Hollett won it from her at cards.
- Seena Hollett gave it to Madrek Orlwood.
- Fedette Orlwood won it from Madrek Orlwood.
- Fedette Orlwood sent it to Islan Lindner.
- After Islan Lindner's death it was handed to Wevie Lindner.
- In Chapter 35 it went from Wevie Lindner to Madan.

The Chapter 35 excerpt gives only the first name "Madan". The surrounding passages in that chapter name Madan Brackwood, so I take that to be the same person.

Answer: Madan Brackwood

The jade ring first belonged to Orvie Hollett (Chapter 1). Later, in Chapter 22, a parcel from Orvie reached Halan Hollett with the jade ring inside, "now his to keep." I found no later change.

Answer: Halan Hollett

- Brevie Hollmere kept it, and on her death it went to Lutho Hollmere.

The only mention of the jade chalice says it belonged to Islan Lindner, head of the Lindner household. A later note says it passes to the holder's eldest living child when the holder dies. Answer: Islan Lindner

3. Jotho the Younger won it from Eldette Corrett at cards.
4. Jotho Corrett gave it to Halan Hollwood.
5. Halan Hollwood gave it to Cotho Hollwood.
6. Cotho Hollwood sent it by carrier to Ortho Corrett, who received it safely.

Ortho Corrett is the current holder, so the holder immediately before was Cotho Hollwood.

Answer: Cotho Hollwood
